articles.description: Companies building flats that they then rent out could usher in big changes for renters.
articles.summary: On Christmas Eve 2021, there was a knock on the door of Lexi Levens' rented flat.
key_points: It was a letter sent by special delivery from the NHS nurse's landlord saying she, her husband, and four children had two months to move out.
Lexi's landlord had used something known then as a Section 21 notice to evict her family without needing to give a reason.
Lexi, along with the housing charity Shelter, went on to lobby the government to improve rights for renters.

articles.summary: BBC secret filming shows dog breeder selling sick puppies for £2k each When Katie Thornton paid £2,000 for a nine-week-old puppy for her son, she knew it was a premium price - but was happy to be doing business with a "legit", council-approved breeder.
key_points: But Ozzy the Dobermann pup started coughing in the car on the way home, and within 48 hours he was in a veterinary hospital receiving urgent treatment for pneumonia.
Since then, his ongoing health problems mean Katie has racked up more than £5,000 in vet bills.
A BBC investigation has found the breeder had been stripped of his five-star rating two months before selling several sick puppies, but continued to advertise as five-star.
